input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 imposes on Customer a non-compete of undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor"), worldwide, running for 24 months after the term, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under this rule (post-term non-compete longer than 12 months and undefined scope) and fails every fallback element. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." No other clause imposes a competitive or field-of-use restriction on Customer (§ 13.4 is ordinary acceptable-use). We therefore take the preferred position and convert § 12.4 into an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete, aligning it with § 12.3.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Convert § 12.4's 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete into an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or businesses we may build, buy or sell, so we have removed the 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete in § 12.4, which also contradicted § 12.3. If you need protection, we could consider a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
